jurisdiction.name: Thailand
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Thailand governs AI through the Cabinet-approved National AI Action Plan 2022-2027, voluntary governance guidance from the Electronic Transactions Development Agency (ETDA) and the digital economy ministry, including a 2024 generative AI governance guideline for organisations, and the Personal Data Protection Act 2019. The Bank of Thailand issued an AI risk management policy guideline for financial institutions in September 2025. A risk-based AI law remains a draft that ETDA is revising after a 2025 public consultation.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The draft AI law and the 2021 AI Ethics Guideline could not be read on official sites and are listed as leads.

instruments.english_title: Thailand National AI Strategy and Action Plan (2022-2027)
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Higher Education, Science, Research and Innovation and Ministry of Digital Economy and Society (approved by the Cabinet)
instruments.current_status: In force for 2022-2027. The title page states the version approved by the Cabinet on 26 July 2565 (2022). A progress deck published on ai.in.th (Key Milestones and Progress, updated June 2026) reports an action plan revision for 2026-2027 after the National AI Committee meeting of 1 May 2025; a follow-on plan for 2028-2032 has been reported but no official document was found (see leads). An English summary is also published on ai.in.th.
instruments.summary: Six-year national AI action plan approved by the Cabinet on 26 July 2022, with the vision of a complete, integrated AI ecosystem that raises the economy and quality of life by 2027. It sets five strategies: preparing society, ethics, law and regulation for AI (ELSI); national AI infrastructure; AI workforce development (at least 30,000 AI personnel); AI technology and innovation; and promoting AI adoption in the public and private sectors, including sandbox mechanisms for AI start-ups. It assigns implementation to a national AI committee and lead agencies under the two proposing ministries.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Current national AI strategy; anchors ETDA's AI governance work, the AI ethics agenda and the draft AI law.
instruments.publisher_name: National Electronics and Computer Technology Center

instruments.english_title: Bank of Thailand Policy Guideline on Artificial Intelligence Risk Management
instruments.issuing_authority: Bank of Thailand (IT Risk Supervision and Examination Department)
instruments.current_status: Issued 12 September 2025 (date on the cover). A draft with the English subtitle 'Guiding Principles for Artificial Intelligence Risk Management' was published by the BOT for public hearing in 2025 (https://www.bot.or.th/content/dam/bot/documents/th/laws-and-rules/hearing/120668%20AI%20Guideline%20public%20hearing.pdf); the final text adds an FAQ annex stating the guideline sets principles that providers apply according to their use.
instruments.summary: Bank of Thailand policy guideline for financial institutions, specialised financial institutions and regulated payment system and payment service operators on managing the risks of AI systems, whether developed in-house or obtained from third parties. It defines AI systems, identifies data, model-development and cyber-threat risks (including prompt injection, model inversion and data poisoning) and sets principles and practices in two parts: governance (board and senior management roles, customer disclosure and human oversight) and development and security controls across the AI lifecycle. It supplements BOT rules on IT risk, third-party risk, data governance and market conduct, and reminds providers that personal data and intellectual property laws still apply.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Sector regulator's AI risk-management expectations for banks and payment providers.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full PDF read (pdftotext), cover dated 12 September 2568 (2025); draft hearing PDF also read.

instruments.english_title: Generative AI Governance Guideline for Organizations
instruments.issuing_authority: Electronic Transactions Development Agency (AI Governance Center) with the Ministry of Digital Economy and Society
instruments.current_status: Announced by MDES and ETDA on 30 October 2024 (ETDA news page dated 30 Oct 2567). The PDF currently served from the ETDA e-book page is version 2.0 dated 25 November 2024 (file name). Voluntary guidance.
instruments.summary: Guideline for executives and staff of public and private organisations on governing the use of generative AI. Its five chapters explain generative AI, its benefits and limitations, its risks and how to manage them, models for deploying it in an organisation, and key considerations for governed use, with an appendix containing a sample organisational generative AI use policy. It extends ETDA's AI Governance Guideline for Executives and is voluntary.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: National generative-AI governance guidance from the AI Governance Center.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 63-page PDF read (pdftotext); launch date from ETDA news page https://www.etda.or.th/th/pr-news/AI_Gov_Anual.aspx (30 Oct 2567), which links the e-book page carrying this PDF.

instruments.official_title: Thailand’s AI Governance Guideline for Executive
instruments.english_title: Thailand's AI Governance Guideline for Executives
instruments.issuing_authority: Electronic Transactions Development Agency (AI Governance Center)
instruments.current_status: Published on the ETDA AIGC Research and Recommendation page; only the year 2023 is stated (file name). An ETDA news item of 29 August 2023 describes the Thai-language version 'แนวทางการประยุกต์ใช้ปัญญาประดิษฐ์อย่างมีธรรมาภิบาลสำหรับผู้บริหารองค์กร' as Thailand's first AI governance guideline; the Thai edition file was not located.
instruments.summary: ETDA's first AI governance guideline for organisational leaders, presented as an English-language deck. It sets out a governance framework of three components (AI governance structure, AI strategy including responsible-AI strategy and AI risk management, and AI operation across the lifecycle), restates Thailand's six AI ethics principles, and maps practice to standards such as ISO/IEC 23894 and the NIST AI RMF. It is voluntary guidance for executives of public and private organisations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Baseline national AI governance guideline later extended by the generative AI guideline.

instruments.current_status: 2023 edition (year stated in the file name and by ETDA as the first, baseline year). ETDA and NSTDA released a 2024 follow-up survey on 15 October 2024 (ETDA news page); a Thailand AI Readiness Assessment 2026 is listed on ai.in.th.
instruments.summary: Government study by ETDA and NSTDA measuring the readiness of Thai public and private organisations to adopt AI for digital services, carried out to support the National AI Action Plan 2022-2027. It reports survey results on AI adoption, defines an AI readiness measurement and proposes future programmes and an AI governance framework for adoption. It is the 2023 baseline for later annual readiness surveys.

instruments.issuing_authority: King of Thailand on the advice and consent of the National Legislative Assembly acting as Parliament
instruments.current_status: In force. Section 2 brings the Act into force the day after publication (28 May 2019), except chapters 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 and sections 95-96, which were to apply one year after publication; that later date was postponed by royal decrees (not re-read in this review; the obligations are generally reported to apply from 1 June 2022).
instruments.summary: Thailand's general data protection law, published in the Royal Gazette (vol. 136, part 69 Kor, p. 52) on 27 May 2019. It governs collection, use and disclosure of personal data, including for training and operating AI systems, sets lawful bases, data-subject rights, sensitive-data rules and cross-border transfer conditions, and establishes the Personal Data Protection Committee and its office. It has no AI-specific provisions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that applies to AI training and use.

leads.note: Draft principles for Thailand's first AI law (risk-based, high-risk AI duties) put to public consultation on the Central Law System (law.go.th listeningDetail?survey_id=NTMxNkRHQV9MQVdfRlJPTlRFTkQ=) until 24 June 2025, per ETDA news of 11 June 2025 (https://www.etda.or.th/th/pr-news/law_ai.aspx). law.go.th could not be read (JS app; WebFetch 403), so the draft text and opening date are unverified. The ai.in.th progress deck (June 2026) says ETDA is consolidating the AI Regulation Act 2022 and AI Promotion Act 2023 drafts and revising the consolidated draft before resubmission to the MDES committee. No bill before Parliament found.
